When base-model LLM outputs re-enter generation pipelines, each recursive step compresses \emph{where} text sits in distributional space while leaving \emph{how} it is shaped nearly unchanged.
We identify this asymmetry as \emph{differential depth response} (DDR) and characterize it across eight \textbf{base-model} generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B parameters).
Under nucleus sampling ($p{=}0.9$, $\tau \leq 0.7$), NLL location statistics and lexical diversity drift monotonically with depth (Cohen's $d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) while distributional shape features remain largely near-stationary ($d \leq 0.10$ for core shape features); per-generator validation, convergent effect-size measures, and replication under greedy decoding confirm this partition.
Prior work on iterative generation documents \emph{what converges}; the central finding is \emph{what is preserved}: shape invariance provides the cross-generator reference needed for depth estimation without per-generator calibration.
As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble exploiting DDR achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+, effective resolution: three depth classes) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, surpassing individual baselines and matching multi-detector ensembles at $2.4\times$ lower cost; an end-to-end classifier recovers substantially more (F1\,=\,0.905, 6-gen LOGO), establishing the analytical framework, not the specific features, as the primary contribution.
Instruction tuning compresses DDR structure, bounding current applicability to base models, though end-to-end classifiers recover depth signal under alignment.
\end{abstract}

To address concerns about the sensitivity of the drifting-boundary threshold,
we sweep $|d|$ from $0.10$ to $0.80$ in increments of $0.05$ and record the

\label{app:holdout-split}

Split~A selects \{Pythia-2.8B, Qwen3-1.7B, OLMo, Mistral\} (validation: Pythia-1B, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-8B, Llama);

However, entropy min's binary (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) $d$ values are uniformly below 0.06 across all four split${\times}$subset combinations, consistent with near-stationarity on the task-relevant metric; its pooled $|\rho|$ reflects change concentrated at the gen-0/gen-1 boundary rather than sustained drift.
Five of seven features are unambiguously classified under any reasonable criterion; entropy min's boundary status is resolved by the binary-task $d$ criterion.

Selection and validation subsets produce identical partitions in both splits (Table~\ref{tab:holdout-split}; Figure~\ref{fig:holdout-scatter}).

\label{fig:holdout-scatter}
\end{figure}

\subsection*{Heteroscedasticity Sensitivity}
\label{app:heteroscedasticity}

Levene tests reject equal variance between gen-1 and gen-2+ for drifting features ($p < 10^{-10}$; variance ratios 1.86--2.21).
To verify that the DDR partition is robust to this heteroscedasticity, we supplement pooled Cohen's $d$ with Glass's $\Delta$ (using the gen-1 standard deviation as denominator) and Cliff's $\delta$ (a non-parametric ordinal effect size; Table~\ref{tab:effect-sizes}).

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\caption{Effect size comparison (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+, $N$\,=\,29{,}095). Glass's $\Delta$ uses the gen-1 SD as denominator; Cliff's $\delta$ thresholds follow Romano et al.\ (2006): $|\delta| < 0.147$ negligible, $< 0.33$ small, $< 0.474$ medium, otherwise large.}
\label{tab:effect-sizes}
\begin{tabular}{llrrr}
\toprule
\textbf{Zone} & \textbf{Feature} & \textbf{$|d|$} & \textbf{$|\Delta|$} & \textbf{$|\delta|$} \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Drifting} & ent.\ mean & 1.054 & 1.410 & 0.587 \\
 & TTR & 0.814 & 1.116 & 0.510 \\
 & hapax ratio & 0.735 & 0.936 & 0.528 \\
\midrule
Intermediate & ent.\ std & 0.457 & 0.605 & 0.295 \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Near-stat.} & tail decay & 0.087 & 0.099 & 0.072 \\
 & ent.\ max & 0.062 & 0.065 & 0.021 \\
 & ent.\ min & 0.016 & 0.015 & 0.354$^{\dagger}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\noindent Effect sizes in Table~\ref{tab:effect-sizes} are computed on the binary task (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+); the main text (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}) reports 3-class pooled $d$ values (e.g., hapax ratio $d{=}0.76$), which are slightly larger because the gen-0/gen-1 contrast contributes additional separation.
Glass's $\Delta$ amplifies drifting effects (1.41 vs.\ 1.05 for entropy mean) because gen-2+ variance exceeds gen-1 variance (ratio 2.08), making the pooled Cohen's $d$ conservative.
Near-stationary features remain negligible under both parametric metrics ($|\Delta| \leq 0.099$).
The minimum drifting-to-maximum-near-stationary gap is $9.5\times$ under Glass's $\Delta$ (0.936\,/\,0.099); heteroscedasticity does not erode the partition.
Cliff's $\delta$ classifies all drifting features as ``large'' ($|\delta| > 0.474$) and entropy std as ``small'' ($|\delta|{=}0.295$), consistent with the parametric partition.

\noindent $^{\dagger}$Entropy min's elevated Cliff's $\delta$ (0.354, ``medium'') reflects distributional shape asymmetry between gen-1 and gen-2+ that rank-based statistics detect but location measures do not (Cohen's $d{=}0.016$, Glass's $\Delta{=}0.015$).
This is consistent with its documented boundary status (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}): the gen-0/gen-1 transition produces rank-order shifts that persist into deeper generations without affecting the mean.

\section{Independent-Seed Control}
\label{app:seed-control}

To test for topic-level leakage from shared seeds across generators, we construct an independent-seed evaluation where Pythia-2.8B and OLMo-2-1B use completely disjoint Wikipedia seed pools (500 seeds each, zero overlap).
Each generator produces depth-0 through depth-4 chains on its own seed pool; features are extracted with the same Pythia-410M reference model.
We then train a 7-feature XGBoost classifier on one generator's data and test on the other, in both directions.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Setting} & \textbf{Binary F1} & \textbf{95\% CI} \\
\midrule
Pythia-2.8B $\rightarrow$ OLMo-2-1B & 0.695 & [0.673, 0.717] \\
OLMo-2-1B $\rightarrow$ Pythia-2.8B & 0.666 & [0.643, 0.689] \\
\midrule
Independent-seed average & 0.680 & --- \\
Shared-seed LOGO (reference) & 0.694 & [0.688, 0.700] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\caption{Independent-seed cross-generator evaluation (binary: gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+). Disjoint seed pools eliminate any possibility of topic-based leakage. The average independent-seed F1 (0.680) is within 1.4\,pp of the shared-seed LOGO baseline (0.694). The classifier thus captures generative degradation patterns rather than seed-specific topic content.}
\label{tab:seed-control}
\end{table}

The small gap ($-$1.4\,pp) between independent-seed and shared-seed evaluation falls within bootstrap confidence intervals, and both directions individually exceed 0.66.
Combined with the seed-level demeaning control (\S\ref{sec:results-classification}), these results provide converging evidence that depth classification is driven by distributional properties of recursive generation, not topic identity.

\paragraph{Semantic similarity analysis.}
Embedding cosine similarity between consecutive depth steps increases monotonically: 0$\rightarrow$1 (0.622), 1$\rightarrow$2 (0.683), 2$\rightarrow$3 (0.801), 3$\rightarrow$4 (0.859).
Deeper generations are thus \emph{more} semantically similar to their inputs, yet the classifier still distinguishes depth classes, suggesting that the depth signal resides in distributional rather than topical properties.
Prompt type modulates the baseline similarity level (continuation 0.717 $<$ elaboration 0.809 $\approx$ rewriting 0.808), plausibly because semantic-preservation constraints reduce topic drift while leaving the distributional location shift intact.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

Recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped, a dichotomy with a mechanistic basis.
Under nucleus sampling, top-$p$ truncation preserves the functional form of the conditional distribution at each step; what changes is the \emph{input}: as the model conditions on increasingly self-typical outputs, expected NLL compresses monotonically.
This yields two testable predictions: (1)~increasing sampling randomness should weaken the location drift, and (2)~semantic-preservation constraints should attenuate it.
Both are confirmed: at $t{=}1.0$, location signal collapses ($\rho$: $-0.60 \to -0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}); under elaboration prompts, drift weakens (F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}).
Causal analyses provide supporting evidence: drifting features contribute $5.5\times$ more to classification, with 6/7 exhibiting significant Granger causality over the five-point chain, though the short series length (5 depths) limits formal causal inference (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}).
These results are established under nucleus sampling ($p{=}0.95$); shape features remain stable even at $\tau{=}1.0$ ($d < 0.15$; Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-temp-stability}).
Greedy decoding ($\tau{=}0$) confirms shape stability across all eight generators (mean $|d|{=}0.05$, max $0.14$) while strengthening drifting effects, establishing DDR as an autoregressive property independent of sampling truncation.
Top-$k$ sampling ($k{=}50$) preserves the full DDR partition for five of eight generators (all non-Pythia/OLMo families), with drifting-feature compression of 10--22\%; the three generators showing elevated shape $d$ exhibit comparable violations under nucleus sampling, indicating model-intrinsic boundary effects rather than strategy-induced degradation (Appendix~\ref{app:decoding-strategy}).

The classifier is a proof-of-concept for corpus-level auditing, not per-document filtering: gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 is insufficient for individual flagging but supports batch-level contamination estimation (${\pm}3$--$4$\% at $n{=}1{,}000$; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
The three-class resolution enables depth-stratified corpus curation (retaining gen-1 content while flagging recursively degraded material), a distinction invisible to binary classifiers.
Depth-aware filtering can serve as a prophylactic against model collapse \cite{drayson_detection_prevents_collapse}, though depth-stratified curation does not yet improve downstream training (TOST equivalence at $\varepsilon{=}{\pm}2\%$; Appendix~\ref{app:downstream}); the primary value lies in provenance, not training improvement.

DDR is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}: retraining erodes tail coverage by updating weights, whereas inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only location, leaving shape stable.
Prior work establishes \emph{that} convergence occurs, from attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains} to diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, without decomposing what drifts from what is preserved.
